raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

When Kimi K3 starts directly with a response, streaming can leave `content` empty and fail to signal when JSON constraints should start. This fix recognizes the response control tokens while preserving ordinary text that quotes the same markers.

We encountered JSON response-format failures during endpoint validation with Moonshot AI's official [Kimi Vendor Verifier (KVV)](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/Kimi-Vendor-Verifier). Those failures prompted this investigation; the CPU reproduction below isolates the vLLM parser defect addressed here.

## Claims

- Route response-only output to `content` and identify the constraint start, including when the response opener spans decode steps.
- Keep quoted marker text in reasoning until the explicit think close, and preserve response-marker text inside JSON strings.
- Preserve explicit unfinished thinking, prompt-level reasoning detection and final reasoning-token counting.

## Validation

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Related K3 reasoning/tool suites | 83 passed; no test-case skips |
| Selected structured-output and plugin-compatibility cases | 47 passed, 1 existing expected failure; 8 other cases not selected |
| Fixed-output HTTP/SDK replay | 48 requests; all 24 candidate responses returned the intended JSON and matching completion-token usage |
| Code quality | Applicable pre-commit hooks, including mypy, passed |

The regressions cover the streaming transition, quoted marker text and the engine's constraint boundary. The engine cases use a custom assistant header, both committed/uncommitted tokens, and a think-close marker spanning the prompt/output boundary. The K3 tests are consolidated into three focused functions rather than a chunking matrix. One manager regression verifies that `**kwargs`-only plugins receive no new arguments; the existing manager and K3 tests cover the other call shapes.

The HTTP replay uses the pinned official tokenizer, real vLLM response generators, ASGI and the OpenAI SDK with fixed outputs. Six baseline response-only streaming requests reproduce missing content. Configured tool-parser cases use `tool_choice="none"`; they do not establish active tool-calling coverage.

The full structured-output suite was not completed locally: Outlines/native-platform cases remain for Linux CI; the unchanged Guidance EOS case is expected to fail. The selected manager tests exercise actual XGrammar/Guidance backends, while the K3-specific regression checks the constraint boundary. Real K3 inference and K3 grammar-mask sampling have not been exercised. Test/replay counts overlap and are not additive.

<details>
<summary>Test selections and lint command</summary>

Pytest selection used after rebasing:

```text
tests/reasoning/test_kimi_k3_reasoning_parser.py tests/tool_use/test_kimi_k3_tool_parser.py tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py -k 'not outlines and not rejected_draft' -q
```

```bash
.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files vllm/reasoning/kimi_k3_reasoning_parser.py tests/reasoning/test_kimi_k3_reasoning_parser.py vllm/v1/structured_output/__init__.py tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Minimal CPU reproduction and regression controls</summary>

Run in a dependency-prepared vLLM source checkout with `.venv/bin/python`; use `PYTHONPATH=.` if running a saved snippet. This loads the pinned official tokenizer, without model weights. The first assertion reproduces missing streamed content. The remaining assertions check quoted text and the engine's constraint-start boundary.

```python
from transformers import AutoTokenizer
from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
from vllm.parser.kimi_k3 import KimiK3Parser
from vllm.reasoning.kimi_k3_reasoning_parser import KimiK3ReasoningParser

class ReasoningOnlyK3(KimiK3Parser):
    reasoning_parser_cls = KimiK3ReasoningParser

tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(
    "moonshotai/Kimi-K3",
    revision="f831ab66814297da540d832a5235f8e904f29d06",
    trust_remote_code=True,
)
parser = ReasoningOnlyK3(tokenizer)
request = ChatCompletionRequest(model="kimi-k3", messages=[])

# Main baseline fails this response-only streaming assertion.
body = '{"ok":true}'
ids = tokenizer.encode("<|open|>response<|sep|>" + body)
content = ""
for index, token_id in enumerate(ids):
    delta = parser.parse_delta(
        tokenizer.decode([token_id]), [token_id], request,
        finished=index == len(ids) - 1,
    )
    if delta:
        content += delta.content or ""
assert content == body

# Control: quoted ordinary text must remain reasoning.
parser = ReasoningOnlyK3(tokenizer)
quoted = "<|open|>response<|sep|> is only a quoted example."
first = parser.parse_delta(
    quoted, tokenizer.encode(quoted, allow_special_tokens=False),
    request, finished=False,
)
assert first.reasoning == quoted and first.content is None

suffix = '<|close|>think<|sep|><|open|>response<|sep|>{"ok":true}'
second = parser.parse_delta(
    suffix, tokenizer.encode(suffix), request, finished=True,
)
assert second.content == '{"ok":true}'

# Ordinary response-marker text inside JSON must survive token-by-token delivery.
parser = ReasoningOnlyK3(tokenizer)
body = '{"marker":"<|open|>response<|sep|>"}'
ids = (tokenizer.encode("<|open|>response<|sep|>")
       + tokenizer.encode(body, allow_special_tokens=False)
       + tokenizer.encode("<|close|>response<|sep|>"))
content = ""
for index, token_id in enumerate(ids):
    delta = parser.parse_delta(
        tokenizer.decode([token_id]), [token_id], request,
        finished=index == len(ids) - 1,
    )
    if delta:
        content += delta.content or ""
assert content == body

# The engine has an explicit prompt/output boundary; the template can vary.
from types import SimpleNamespace
from vllm.sampling_params import SamplingParams, StructuredOutputsParams
from vllm.v1.request import Request
from vllm.v1.structured_output import StructuredOutputManager

prompt = tokenizer.encode(
    '<|open|>message role="assistant" custom="x"<|sep|><|open|>think<|sep|>'
)
engine_request = Request(
    request_id="repro", prompt_token_ids=prompt,
    sampling_params=SamplingParams(
        max_tokens=32, structured_outputs=StructuredOutputsParams(json_object=True),
    ), pooling_params=None,
)
reasoner = KimiK3ReasoningParser(tokenizer)
manager = SimpleNamespace(enable_in_reasoning=False, _get_reasoner=lambda _: reasoner)
opener = tokenizer.encode("<|open|>response<|sep|>")
delta_ids = opener + tokenizer.encode("{}", allow_special_tokens=False)
assert StructuredOutputManager._get_constraint_bounds(
    manager, engine_request, delta_ids,
).constraint_start == len(opener)

# Invalid speculative suffixes must not hide the first genuine transition.
proposal = opener + opener + tokenizer.encode("{}", allow_special_tokens=False)
assert StructuredOutputManager._get_constraint_bounds(
    manager, engine_request, proposal,
).constraint_start == len(opener)
```

Main fails the response-only content and constraint-start assertions. This change passes all assertions, including the quotation controls. The tokenizer encodes structural markers differently from the same characters in ordinary text. These are constructed token sequences, not captured model outputs.

</details>

## Details

The streaming extractor and constraint-start check rely on think markers. A completion that starts with a response has no generated think close, so they miss the initial response transition.

Moonshot's [tokenizer](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3/blob/f831ab66814297da540d832a5235f8e904f29d06/tokenization_kimi.py#L154) distinguishes response control tokens from ordinary text containing the same characters. Checking token IDs for this transition prevents quoted reasoning from leaking into `content`; the check stays local to K3 and does not scan the full prompt on each decoding step.

The frontend and engine share the K3 response-prefix predicate. The engine supplies its current prompt length only to methods that explicitly declare the keyword-only `prompt_len` parameter, using the existing cached `supports_kw` helper. The shared manager has no K3 import or model-class check. Existing two-argument and `**kwargs`-only plugins retain their original calls; the base `ReasoningParser` interface is unchanged. Full input remains available for think-close markers spanning the prompt/output boundary. The response-prefix check reads only the fixed marker-length slice, and the [encoder's explicit think-close rule](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3/blob/f831ab66814297da540d832a5235f8e904f29d06/encoding_k3.py#L505) is retained.

Limits: the unchanged non-streaming text extractor still misparses ordinary think-marker characters inside JSON strings. That is a separate pre-existing issue. Active tool calling is outside the checked serving coverage. The tested endpoint's backend/version was unavailable, so this fix does not establish the cause of all observed KVV failures.

Related reports: [#57688](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57688) and [#57714](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57714).

Related PRs: [#57689](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57689) and [#57718](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57718) address response-only streaming and the constraint start. In a CPU replay of their compared revisions together, ordinary response-marker text quoted at the start of reasoning entered `content`, making the final JSON invalid. This change checks control-token IDs, keeping that quotation in reasoning and the JSON intact.

<details>
<summary>Source baseline</summary>

- Source baseline: [8352b242](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/8352b2427f704652da1910f0d53f3fdcc2fa2b0d). The current change is based on [189bbfb9](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/189bbfb9f432e283e21dcdf2a78357ae5db05ace); the follow-up uses an explicit prompt offset instead of matching a template header.
- Compared PR revisions: #57689 [a80adb5b](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57689/commits/a80adb5bf40da8e7ffd138e6a5a7ca1a5fec85e3) and #57718 [d3e71167](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57718/commits/d3e71167aa76290a34fc2c128d701bd6359732ff), mechanically rebased onto the comparison baseline.

</details>

AI assistance was used for implementation, tests and drafting this PR.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Targeted K3 regressions, the CPU MRE and fixed-output replay pass; selected manager checks and remaining CI/serving gaps are listed above.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.

</details>

Thanks for the detailed repro. I left two inline comments.

One more point about scope. The test diff is about 175 lines: six new tests plus a 3×2×2 parametrize matrix, for a 39-line fix. Several cases also overlap: response-only content, quoted-marker JSON and the split opener are each covered more than once. AGENTS.md asks to keep tests minimal ("if the test diff dwarfs the code change, cut scope"). Could you trim this down to three cases: the response-only transition, the quoted opener staying in reasoning, and the engine constraint-start case?

This copies the generation prompt (`<|open|>message role="assistant"<|sep|><|open|>think<|sep|>`) into the parser and requires the response opener to come right after it. The frontend side (`extract_reasoning_streaming`) only checks that the output starts with `<|open|>response<|sep|>`. With the current Moonshot encoder and the Rust renderer the two agree; I checked that the rendered prompt tail is token-for-token identical. But they agree only because the template happens to match this literal. If the assistant header changes (a custom `--chat-template`, a hand-built prompt, or a template update that adds an attribute to the assistant message), the frontend will still route a response-only reply to `content`, while the engine never sets `reasoning_ended`. Then `response_format` / `json_schema` is not enforced for that request, and nothing raises an error.

What both sides actually mean is "the response opener is the first generated token". The engine already knows where the output starts, so it would be more robust to check `response_start == num_prompt_tokens` there (or have the structured-output manager pass the output-only view) instead of matching a copied template string. That would also let the frontend and engine share one predicate.

The `delta_text` arm of this conditional can't run on the real streaming path. The step that completes the opener also has `_is_reasoning_end_streaming` see `<|open|>response<|sep|>` at output index 0 (window_start is 0, so response_start == 0). That flips `state.reasoning_ended`, and `DelegatingParser` never calls `extract_reasoning_streaming` again. So every time this branch runs, `len(previous_token_ids) < len(self._response_open_ids)`.

I checked this by streaming the opener plus a JSON body through `KimiK3Parser.parse_delta` with the test `DummyTokenizer` and 3000 random chunkings. The `delta_text` case never came up.

Suggest dropping the conditional:

```python
if response_open is not None:
    return DeltaMessage(content=current_text or None)
```

inline_comments.body:
This copies the generation prompt (`<|open|>message role="assistant"<|sep|><|open|>think<|sep|>`) into the parser and requires the response opener to come right after it. The frontend side (`extract_reasoning_streaming`) only checks that the output starts with `<|open|>response<|sep|>`. With the current Moonshot encoder and the Rust renderer the two agree; I checked that the rendered prompt tail is token-for-token identical. But they agree only because the template happens to match this literal. If the assistant header changes (a custom `--chat-template`, a hand-built prompt, or a template update that adds an attribute to the assistant message), the frontend will still route a response-only reply to `content`, while the engine never sets `reasoning_ended`. Then `response_format` / `json_schema` is not enforced for that request, and nothing raises an error.

What both sides actually mean is "the response opener is the first generated token". The engine already knows where the output starts, so it would be more robust to check `response_start == num_prompt_tokens` there (or have the structured-output manager pass the output-only view) instead of matching a copied template string. That would also let the frontend and engine share one predicate.

inline_comments.body:
The `delta_text` arm of this conditional can't run on the real streaming path. The step that completes the opener also has `_is_reasoning_end_streaming` see `<|open|>response<|sep|>` at output index 0 (window_start is 0, so response_start == 0). That flips `state.reasoning_ended`, and `DelegatingParser` never calls `extract_reasoning_streaming` again. So every time this branch runs, `len(previous_token_ids) < len(self._response_open_ids)`.

I checked this by streaming the opener plus a JSON body through `KimiK3Parser.parse_delta` with the test `DummyTokenizer` and 3000 random chunkings. The `delta_text` case never came up.

Suggest dropping the conditional:

```python
if response_open is not None:
    return DeltaMessage(content=current_text or None)
```

Thanks for the concrete review. I've addressed both inline points and reduced the K3 regressions to the three requested cases. I chose the existing `supports_kw` helper for the manager boundary so this change doesn't need a K3 special case or a new base-parser interface. Validation and the explicit AI-assistance statement are now in the description.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks for the detailed repro. I left two inline comments.

One more point about scope. The test diff is about 175 lines: six new tests plus a 3×2×2 parametrize matrix, for a 39-line fix. Several cases also overlap: response-only content, quoted-marker JSON and the split opener are each covered more than once. AGENTS.md asks to keep tests minimal ("if the test diff dwarfs the code change, cut scope"). Could you trim this down to three cases: the response-only transition, the quoted opener staying in reasoning, and the engine constraint-start case?
